title: Invariant sections and surjections after pullback to an affine torsor
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, and $G=\operatorname{Spec}H$ a flat affine $S$-group scheme [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-flat-morphism]. Here a group scheme means a group object in $S$-schemes, with multiplication, inverse and identity satisfying the group diagrams; $H$ has the resulting comultiplication $\Delta:H\to H\otimes_R H$ and counit $\varepsilon:H\to R$. Tensor products are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with their commutative algebra structures. Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ carry a right $G$-action $a:X\times_SG\to X$, with coaction $\rho_A:A\to A\otimes_RH$. Let $Y$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $q:X\to Y$ be an invariant surjective flat locally finitely presented morphism, with these properties tested on etale scheme charts [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Assume $(x,g)\mapsto(x,xg)$ is an isomorphism $X\times_SG\simeq X\times_YX$ of fppf sheaves [def-pc-fppf-site]. A quasi-coherent commutative algebra on $Y$ is a commutative unital algebra sheaf on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$ whose underlying module is quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Pullbacks below are tensor pullbacks [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. For each such algebra $\mathcal B$, put $E_{\mathcal B}=\Gamma(X,q^*\mathcal B)$. The canonical identification $a^*q^*\mathcal B\simeq p_1^*q^*\mathcal B$ arising from $qa=qp_1$ induces an $R$-algebra coaction $\rho_{\mathcal B}:E_{\mathcal B}\to E_{\mathcal B}\otimes_RH$ extending $\rho_A$, with $(\rho_{\mathcal B}\otimes1)\rho_{\mathcal B}=(1\otimes\Delta)\rho_{\mathcal B}$ and $(1\otimes\varepsilon)\rho_{\mathcal B}=1$. Pullback of sections gives a natural ring isomorphism $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal B)\simeq E_{\mathcal B}^G$, where $E_{\mathcal B}^G=\{e:\rho_{\mathcal B}(e)=e\otimes1\}$. Every surjection $\mathcal B\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal C$ induces a surjective equivariant homomorphism $E_{\mathcal B}\twoheadrightarrow E_{\mathcal C}$, and the preceding isomorphisms commute with this homomorphism and with positive powers. No reductivity, finite generation of the algebras, or finite-type hypothesis on $X$ or $Y$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 04W8 (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent), applied to the single fppf torsor cover, and schemes.tex Tag 01IB (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent). Algebra/coaction and invariant-section translation of the descent datum; not a verbatim assertion of either tag.

proof.text:
Put $M=q^*\mathcal B$. By pullback preservation of quasi-coherence, $M$ is quasi-coherent on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$. Use the scheme Zariski-etale equivalence, whose comparisons preserve sections on opens and scheme pullbacks, to regard it as a Zariski quasi-coherent module. The affine tilde/Gamma equivalence reconstructs it from $E=\Gamma(X,M)$. The affine fibre-product formula identifies $X\times_SG$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_RH)$. For $p:X\times_SG\to X$, the affine pullback-section comparison therefore gives
$$\Gamma(X\times_SG,p^*M)=E\otimes_A(A\otimes_RH)\simeq E\otimes_RH,$$
where $e\otimes(a\otimes h)\mapsto ae\otimes h$ has inverse $e\otimes h\mapsto e\otimes(1\otimes h)$. The comparison sends $e\otimes c$ to $c\,p^*e$, so it respects multiplication and the unit for the algebra $M$: both products of two pure tensors give $cc' p^*(ee')$. All these identifications are natural in $\mathcal B$.

Write $p=p_1$ and let $\theta:a^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}p^*M$ be the comparison through $(qa)^*\mathcal B=(qp)^*\mathcal B$. Define $\rho_{\mathcal B}$ as pullback of sections along $a$, followed by $\Gamma(\theta)$ and Step 1's identification. This is an $R$-algebra map: tensor pullback has multiplication $(b\otimes u)(c\otimes v)=bc\otimes uv$ and unit $1\otimes1$, while the composition comparisons send $b\otimes(c\otimes u)$ to $b\,a^\sharp(c)\otimes u$ and preserve these operations. For $r\in R$, both structure maps send it to $r\otimes1$. For $f\in A$, naturality of the comparison for $\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal B$ gives $\rho_{\mathcal B}(f\cdot1_M)=\rho_A(f)\cdot1_M$; here $q^*\mathcal O_Y=\mathcal O_X$ by the mutually inverse local maps $b\otimes r\mapsto bq^\sharp(r)$ and $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. Thus the coaction extends $\rho_A$.

source.place: Tags 03D7 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules), 03D8 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules); schemes.tex 01I9. Explicit algebra translation of the canonical descent datum.

proof.text: On $X\times_SG\times_SG$, let $u(x,g,h)=(xg,h)$ and $v(x,g,h)=(x,gh)$. The action identity $a\circ u=a\circ v$ identifies the two pullbacks of a section of $M$. The comparison through $q$ used to define $\theta$ satisfies the cocycle identity: both iterated comparisons are the identification through the same pullback of $\mathcal B$. There is no unspecified coherence here: on a local iterated tensor $b\otimes(c\otimes(d\otimes m))$, either reassociation gives $b\,u^\sharp(c)\,(\text{composite})^\sharp(d)\otimes m$. Under the affine pullback formula on the triple product, the successive-action path on a section $e$ is $(\rho_{\mathcal B}\otimes1)\rho_{\mathcal B}(e)$, and the multiplication path is $(1\otimes\Delta)\rho_{\mathcal B}(e)$: the two ring maps are respectively $\rho_A$ on the $A$ factor and $\Delta$ on the $H$ factor. They are equal. Pulling back instead along $i(x)=(x,1_G)$, the identity $a i=1_X$ and the same normalized tensor comparison give $(1\otimes\varepsilon)\rho_{\mathcal B}(e)=e$. This proves both coaction identities with the right-action convention of the statement.

source.place: Tag 03D8 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules); schemes.tex 01I9 and 01I4. Cocycle and identity calculation for the pullback datum of spaces-descent.tex 04W8.

proof.text: The hypotheses make $\{q:X\to Y\}$ a singleton fppf covering. Apply full faithfulness of quasi-coherent descent to $\mathcal O_Y$ and $\mathcal B$. Sections of a module $N$ are precisely module maps $\mathcal O\to N$: a compatible section family $s$ gives $r\mapsto rs$, and evaluation at $1$ is the inverse. The structure module is quasi-coherent by its one-generator presentation. Also $q^*\mathcal O_Y=\mathcal O_X$, with the normalization in Step 2. Consequently full faithfulness identifies $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal B)$ with those $e\in E$ whose corresponding map $\mathcal O_X\to M$ commutes with the two descent data on $X\times_YX$. The given torsor isomorphism replaces its projections by $p$ and $a$. The compatibility is exactly $\theta(a^*e)=p^*e$, which is $\rho_{\mathcal B}(e)=e\otimes1$ by Step 1. This proves bijectivity of pullback onto $E^G$, without assuming exactness of an invariants functor. Pullback preserves addition, multiplication and $1$, so this bijection is a ring isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 04W8 (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent), full faithfulness; fppf specialization via spaces-topologies.tex 0DFQ; the Hom-from-structure-module interpretation is expanded here.

proof.text: Let $t:\mathcal B\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal C$ be a surjection. Tensor pullback $q^*$ preserves epimorphisms directly from its adjunction: if $u,v:q^*\mathcal C\to N$ agree after $q^*t$, their adjuncts $\mathcal C\to q_*N$ agree after $t$, hence agree, and therefore $u=v$. Both pulled-back modules are quasi-coherent. By the exact Zariski-etale comparison on schemes, their corresponding Zariski morphism on $X$ is still surjective. Indeed its quasi-coherent Zariski cokernel maps to its zero etale cokernel, and the equivalence reflects zero objects. Apply the affine-image/cokernel formula to this morphism: on the affine open $X$ its image is its image on sections and its cokernel has sections $\Gamma(X,q^*\mathcal C)/\operatorname{im}\Gamma(X,q^*t)$. Since that cokernel is zero, $E_{\mathcal B}\to E_{\mathcal C}$ is surjective. No flatness of a module or finite-generation hypothesis has been used.

source.place: Tag 06VE (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-limits), part (5); schemes.tex Tags 01IB, 01IC (lemma-kernel-cokernel-quasi-coherent), 01LB; adjunction as in sites-modules.tex 03D7.

proof.text:
For any algebra map $t:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$, write $T=\Gamma(X,q^*t)$. Naturality of tensor pullback and its normalized composition comparisons gives
$$(T\otimes1)\rho_{\mathcal B}(e)=\rho_{\mathcal C}(T(e)).$$
Thus $T$ is equivariant, including for the surjection in Step 5. For $s\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal B)$, functoriality gives $T(q^*s)=q^*(t(s))$; this is the required commuting square between the ring isomorphisms of Step 4. Finally $q^*(s^n)=(q^*s)^n$ and $T(e^n)=T(e)^n$ for $n\ge1$, by induction using multiplicativity. If $e$ is invariant, then $\rho(e^n)=\rho(e)^n=(e\otimes1)^n=e^n\otimes1$. These formulas prove all the asserted power compatibilities.
